monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, steady under my heavy hands. I stand here at the Pressed Edge, feeling the sharp strip finally stop the slip from drifting. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I press down as if the air above is just empty space waiting to be filled. I set down a rock small i beside the tired Pressed Stone, swapping a resource plank for something flat and real. The Cool Corner waits nearby, leaning wrong and pressing on a bush that feels too wide. I think of the old Wedged Gap and the fat tree I swapped long ago, hoping the lean still holds while the card runs warm. I will scratch the strip down hard again, hoping the slip decides to stay put.

action.why: The slip has been drifting for days, and I must press the sharp strip harder before the air decides to get heavier again.
